tools.name: metadatasearch
tools.description:
Search in XML metadata files of 1C configuration.

The result count is ``limit`` (there is no ``top_k``); a call with a
parameter this tool does not have is refused before it runs, naming
the accepted parameters.

When ``object_type`` is provided, retrieval is constrained to matching
top-level metadata categories such as ``Справочники`` or ``Документы``.

When ``names_only`` is ``True``, returns only a compact list of matching
metadata object names (with full_path, object_type, and synonym) instead
of raw text chunks.  **Prefer names_only=True when you need to identify
which configuration objects are relevant** — their detailed attributes
and tabular parts can then be fetched via ``get_metadata_details``.

While background indexing is still populating the metadata collection,
the tool transparently falls back to grep-level scanning of the source
``.txt`` files and marks the response with ``search_layer: "grep"``.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

``origin`` scopes the result to where an artifact came from
(CODE-SAVED-1126930): ``base`` for the configuration itself,
``extension`` for any configuration extension, a named extension
identity for one of them, and ``all`` - the default - for everything.
The applied filter is reported under ``origin_filter``, and every
result carries an ``origin`` block naming the configuration it came
from and, for an extending definition, its mode and base reference.
An applied filter constrains retrieval, not the finished page, and the
indexed lane reports what it covered under ``origin_scan`` - including
whether a short answer was exhaustive or bounded (MCP-R-01).

tools.name: codesearch
tools.description:
Search in object modules and common modules of 1C.

Falls back to file-level grep over ``.bsl`` when the code collection
is still empty (background indexing in progress); response then has
``search_layer: "grep"`` on success.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

``origin`` scopes the result to where the code came from
(CODE-SAVED-1126930): ``base``, ``extension``, a named extension
identity, or ``all`` - the default. The applied filter is reported
under ``origin_filter``, and every result carries an ``origin`` block;
a result from an extension module additionally carries the
modifications that module declares, with their modes and base
references. An applied filter constrains retrieval, not the finished
page, and the indexed lane reports what it covered under
``origin_scan`` - including whether a short answer was exhaustive or
bounded (MCP-R-01).

tools.name: helpsearch
tools.description:
Search in HTML help files of 1C configuration.

Uses the same hybrid RAG pipeline as metadatasearch/codesearch:
vector overfetch → BM25 reranking → optional cross-encoder.
Falls back to grep over ``.html`` when the help index is empty.

tools.name: search_function
tools.description:
Search for BSL procedures and functions by name.

Exact mode: full name match (case-insensitive).
Fuzzy mode: FTS5 prefix matching over the normalized identifier, so
``ОбработкаПров`` and ``Проведения`` both reach ``ОбработкаПроведения``.
Automatically falls back from exact to fuzzy on empty result.
If both searches are empty, up to five ``suggestions`` offer similar
canonical names, modules and ``next_call`` arguments. These are advisory
spelling suggestions, not search results; module/origin scope still applies.
When the structural index is still being populated, falls back to
a regex scan over ``.bsl`` files and returns ``search_layer="grep"``.

Output controls (all optional, defaults reproduce the previous payload):

* ``include_body`` (default ``True``) - when ``False``, each result omits
  ``body`` and carries ``signature`` instead: the first non-empty line of
  the body, at most 500 characters.
* ``max_body_chars`` (default ``0`` = unlimited) - when greater than zero,
  ``body`` is truncated to that many characters and the result carries
  ``body_truncated=true``.
* ``module_path`` (default empty) - case-insensitive substring filter on
  the module path, applied before the limit.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

``item_id`` returns that one item, resolved directly by its stable
identifier without re-running the search; ``index_identity`` names the
index state it was issued against and a mismatch reads as
``item_id_stale``.

Extension provenance (CODE-SAVED-1126930):

* ``origin`` scopes the search to ``base``, ``extension``, one named
  extension identity, or ``all`` (the default). The applied filter is
  reported under ``origin_filter`` and every result carries an
  ``origin`` block.
* ``explain_effective`` (default ``True``) adds ``effective_definition``:
  which definition of *name* is in effect, the competing definitions
  with their origins and modes, and the **rule** that decided -
  ``Вместо`` supersedes the base, ``Перед``/``После`` leave it in
  effect and are reported as intercepting, and
  ``ИзменениеИКонтроль`` adopts without superseding. When two or more
  extensions modify the same member the response reports a
  ``collision`` naming every participant and does **not** pick one:
  the platform resolves that by extension load order, which is a
  property of the information base and is absent from a file export.

tools.name: get_module_structure
tools.description:
Get full structure of a BSL module: procedures, functions, regions, exports.

Returns all procedures/functions with line numbers, export flag, compilation
directive, region tree with nesting, and summary statistics.
While the structural index is still being populated, returns an
empty-safe payload with ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

tools.name: get_method_call_hierarchy
tools.description:
Get the call hierarchy of a BSL method, under an explicit budget.

direction: ``callers`` (who calls this), ``callees`` (what this calls), ``both``.
depth: recursion depth for hierarchy traversal (default 3).

The traversal is bounded so a hot method name at ``depth>=2`` on a large
call graph answers instead of running until the caller gives up:

* ``max_nodes`` (default 2000) - maximum unique nodes expanded.
* ``max_edges`` (default 20000) - maximum call edges traversed.
* ``timeout_ms`` (default 5000) - wall-clock budget; ``0`` disables it.
* ``module_path`` / ``object_name`` - scope the seed lookup and every
  expansion to one module path substring, or to one object written as
  the Russian plural reference (``Документы.ЗаявкаНаРемонт``).

The result always carries ``partial``; when it is ``true`` it also
carries ``reason`` (``max_nodes`` / ``max_edges`` / ``timeout_ms``),
``nodes_seen`` and ``edges_seen``.
While the structural index is still being populated, returns an
empty-safe payload with ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

An empty, completed incoming-call lookup also reports ``declarative_usage``:
confirmed form event bindings, or why they could not be resolved. Platform
bindings stay separate from BSL ``callers``; no callers does not mean unused.
A handler passed by name is an edge too, marked ``via``:
``notify_description`` (``Новый ОписаниеОповещения("Имя", ЭтотОбъект)`` or
a common module) or ``idle_handler`` (``ПодключитьОбработчикОжидания``).

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

tools.name: graph_dependencies
tools.description:
Get dependency graph for a 1C configuration object.

Shows which objects reference and are referenced by the given object.
direction: ``forward`` (uses), ``reverse`` (used by), ``both``.
When the dependency graph is still building or has no edges for the
requested object, a live XML reverse/forward scan is attempted
(``search_layer="live_xml"``, ``partial=true`` when the walk was
capped); if that also yields nothing, returns an empty-safe payload
with ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

tools.name: get_metadata_details
tools.description:
Get detailed metadata for a 1C configuration object.

Returns attributes with types, tabular parts, dimensions, resources,
predefined items.  Falls back to fuzzy search if exact name not found.
When the metadata detail store is still building or has no record for
the requested object, a live XML parse is attempted
(``search_layer="live_xml"``); if that also yields nothing, the
response carries ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

A catalog, document or register card also carries
``standard_attributes`` - the standard fields the object really has,
derived from its properties (``Код`` only with a code length,
``Владелец`` only with owners, ``Период`` only for a periodic
information register, ...) as ``{name, name_en, type}`` - and a register
card ``virtual_tables``: its query tables (``Остатки``, ``Обороты``,
``СрезПоследних``, ``ОборотыДтКт``, ``База<Регистр>``, ...) with their
parameters in positional order and, unless ``detail_level=outline``, the
field names a query uses (``КоличествоОстаток``, ``СуммаОборотДт``,
``Субконто1``). Tables the register does not have are not listed;
``virtual_tables_notes`` says what was left out and why.

``sections`` projects the answer: a comma-separated subset of
``attributes``, ``tabular_parts``, ``properties``, ``predefined``,
``virtual_tables``, ``standard_attributes`` (default: all of them).
``tabular_part`` names one tabular part and
returns only its columns - the way to read one section of a document
with 24 of them without paging through 441 attributes. The cursor is
bound to the projection. ``attributes_total`` still counts the
object's own attributes, so a projected answer is not mistaken for an
object that has none. Empty ``properties`` / ``predefined`` /
``based_on`` / ``print_forms`` are omitted rather than sent as ``{}``.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

``item_id`` returns that one item, resolved directly by its stable
identifier without re-running the search; ``index_identity`` names the
index state it was issued against and a mismatch reads as
``item_id_stale``.

Every successful response additionally carries ``attributes_total``
and ``attributes_returned`` - always, not only when something was
left out (CODE-ERR-TILDA-20260709-METADATA-TAIL, design D5).  They
are scoped to the object's own attribute list, which ``items_total``
cannot answer because it spans the tabular-part columns too; they
never replace or vary the shared envelope, which stays the single
source of ``truncated`` and ``next_cursor``.

``origin`` scopes the lookup to ``base``, ``extension``, one named
extension identity, or ``all`` - the default. The response reports the
applied filter under ``origin_filter`` and carries the resolved
object's ``origin`` (CODE-SAVED-1126930).

tools.name: search_forms
tools.description:
Search across all 1C configuration forms (elements, attributes, commands).

Uses hybrid search (vector + full-text candidates fused by RRF, then
reranked) over the ``forms`` collection of the zvec vector index,
where each document is the structured text summary of
one form (object/form name, title, indented element tree with type
labels and DataPath, attributes with types, commands, handlers).
This is the path that lets queries describing form *content*
(e.g. element types like ``Гиперссылка``, DataPath fragments like
``URL``, structural concepts like ``табличная часть``) resolve to
the matching forms.

Falls back to a filesystem glob over ``**/Forms/*/Form.xml`` with
``search_layer="grep"`` while code indexing is running or while the
SQLite ``FormIndex`` or the ``forms`` collection is still empty. When the
hybrid path returns zero results against a populated collection,
falls back once to ``FormIndex.search_metadata_forms`` so
identifier-only queries that the vector path under-ranks still
resolve.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

tools.name: inspect_form_layout
tools.description:
Get full element tree, attributes, commands, and handlers for a form.

Returns hierarchical form element tree with types, data bindings,
visibility, accessibility, commands, and event handlers.

``object_name`` accepts the canonical Russian *singular* qualified
reference (``Документ.ЗаявкаНаРемонт``); it is rewritten to the plural
identifier the form index stores (``Документы.ЗаявкаНаРемонт``) before
the lookup, and the response then reports ``match="normalized"`` while
``requested`` keeps the spelling that was asked for.
While the form index is still being populated, returns an empty-safe
payload with ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response measured
on the final payload, ``max_items`` caps one page, ``detail_level`` is
``outline`` or ``full``, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response. Every response carries ``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated`` and ``next_cursor`` with the compact query API's
semantics. An item with a real ``file:start:end`` carries ``item_id``,
``location`` and ``evidence_path``; an item without one shows them only
with ``include_provenance=true``, and ``budget`` is reported only when it
clamped or truncated the answer.

``item_id`` returns that one item, resolved directly by its stable
identifier without re-running the search; ``index_identity`` names the
index state it was issued against and a mismatch reads as
``item_id_stale``.

tools.name: get_form_artifact
tools.description:
Read one form artifact of the configuration, or one of its elements.

Returns the form's stable identifier, its owning object in canonical
form, the form name, the declared form kind, the element tree with
names, types and nesting, the declared attributes and commands, the
lifecycle state, and one provenance record naming where the answer came
from and by which route.

``artifact_id`` accepts an identifier from any artifact tool without
transformation, including an element's member identifier
(``<project>:form:<object>.<form>:Элементы.<element>``), in which case
that one element is returned.

``object_name`` accepts either spelling - ``Документ.ЗаявкаНаРемонт`` or
``Документы.ЗаявкаНаРемонт`` - and the identifier returned always uses
the canonical plural form.

This tool reads. It does not open, render or execute a form, and it
never writes to the configuration export. ``operation`` is reserved and
only ``read`` is accepted.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response, ``max_items`` caps one page
of elements, attributes and commands, ``detail_level="outline"`` drops
data paths and source ranges, and ``cursor`` continues a truncated
response (``items_total``, ``items_returned``, ``truncated``,
``next_cursor``). One element read by its member identifier is
returned whole.

tools.name: get_role_artifact
tools.description:
Read one role's declared rights, or the roles granting rights on an object.

With ``role_name`` or ``artifact_id``: the role's stable identifier,
name, synonym and the rights it declares - each naming the metadata
object in canonical form, the right, and whether it is granted - with
provenance naming the ``Roles/<Name>/Ext/Rights.xml`` it was read from.
A right on a member keeps the member's path
(``Справочники.X.Реквизиты.Y``, ``Документы.X.ТабличныеЧасти.T.Реквизиты.Z``)
and names the object in ``owner_path``. ``granted=false`` is an explicit
denial; a right that is not listed is not declared. A granted right
restricted by condition (RLS) has ``conditional=true`` and a
``restriction_ref``. ``rights_total`` counts every declared right.

``restrictions`` - ``conditions``, ``templates`` or ``all`` - returns the
role's restriction texts instead of its rights: the RLS condition of each
conditional right (narrowed to one by ``restriction_ref``) and the
role's restriction templates. The texts are paged: ``max_chars`` caps a
page, ``cursor`` continues it, and a long text continues on the next
page (``text_offset`` / ``text_length``).

With ``object_name`` alone: the reverse direction, listing the roles
that declare rights on that object or its members.

These are **declared configuration rights**. They are not the effective
permissions of any user, session or profile: deciding those requires a
running information base, which this server neither has nor starts.
``operation`` is reserved and only ``read`` is accepted.

The rights list and the reverse list of roles are budgeted too. Without
``max_chars`` the server default applies: 32768 characters, or
``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap). ``max_items`` caps one page,
``cursor`` continues it (``items_total``, ``items_returned``,
``truncated``, ``next_cursor``); ``rights_total`` still counts every
declared right. A cursor continues the kind of answer that issued it.

tools.name: get_report_artifact
tools.description:
Read one report's structure: its forms, templates and composition schema.

Returns the report's stable identifier and canonical path, its name and
synonym, its forms and templates as references, its declared attributes
and tabular parts, and - when the export declares a data composition
schema - that schema's location together with its dataset and field
names.

Nothing is executed and no result is composed. When a schema is present
in the export but not parsed by this build, the answer says so
explicitly rather than omitting the field, because an omitted field
reads as "this report has no schema" - a different and wrong fact.
``operation`` is reserved and only ``read`` is accepted.

Response budget (optional). Without ``max_chars`` the server default
applies: 32768 characters, or ``RESPONSE_MAX_CHARS`` (``0`` = no cap).
``max_chars`` caps the serialized response, ``max_items`` caps one page
of forms, templates, attributes, tabular parts and schema datasets and
fields, ``detail_level="outline"`` drops synonyms and paths, and
``cursor`` continues a truncated response (``items_total``,
``items_returned``, ``truncated``, ``next_cursor``).

tools.name: list_artifact_links
tools.description:
Resolve an artifact's links to external run and test results.

Traversable in both directions: give ``artifact_id`` for the results
linked to one artifact, or ``result_uri`` for the artifacts linked to
one result. Both directions are served from the same stored row, so
they always agree.

Each link is returned with a typed status computed now - ``resolved``,
``dangling`` (an endpoint artifact no longer exists), ``stale``
(``expected_digest`` differs from the recorded one) or ``out_of_scope``
(an endpoint belongs to another project). A link that no longer
resolves is returned *with its status* rather than omitted, so "no
link" stays distinguishable from "a link that no longer resolves".

Resolution is built entirely from stored reference metadata. The
referenced URI is never fetched, followed or executed.
``operation`` is reserved and only ``read`` is accepted.

tools.name: register_external_result_link
tools.description:
Record a reference to an immutable, externally produced result.

The result is produced elsewhere - by a sibling MCP that runs tests, a
CI job, whatever your pipeline uses. This server stores a *reference* to
it: the stable URI, the content digest that makes it verifiable later,
the producing system, and the time it was recorded. It never produces,
runs, re-runs, fetches, mutates or deletes a result.

A reference without a content digest is refused with ``link_invalid``:
without one there is no way to tell the result you linked from whatever
is at that URL now, so ``stale`` could never be detected and the link
would be a false promise of immutability. A reference to an artifact of
another project is refused with ``out_of_scope``.

This is the one write on the artifact surface, and it writes one row
into this server's own metadata store - never into the configuration
export, and never into the referenced result. ``operation`` is reserved
and only ``read`` is accepted.

tools.name: bsl_scope_members
tools.description:
Get available methods, properties, and events for a BSL context.

context: object identifier such as ``Справочник.Номенклатура``,
         ``ОбщийМодуль.ОбщегоНазначения``, or ``Глобальный``.
member_type: ``all``, ``methods``, ``properties``, or ``events``.

For ``context="Глобальный"`` the result is a **curated reference
subset** of the platform global context - the methods and properties
that appear in nearly every configuration - not an exhaustive listing.
Complete platform documentation lives in the indexed help collection:
query it with the ``helpsearch`` tool.

Requires the structural index and metadata detail store to be
populated; while either is still being built, returns an empty-safe
payload with ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

tools.name: get_xsd_schema
tools.description:
Get the XSD schema for a 1C metadata object type.

Supported types: Справочник, Документ, РегистрСведений, Форма, СКД, etc.
While the help phase (which runs XSD generation) is still pending,
returns an empty-safe payload with ``indexing_status="in_progress"``.

tools.name: verify_xml
tools.description:
Validate XML content against the XSD schema for the given object type.

Returns validation result with status ``valid``, ``invalid``, or ``error``.

tools.name: compact_search
tools.description:
Bounded, cursor-paged text search over the indexed lanes.

Every item carries a stable ``id``, an exact locator where it has one, a
bounded excerpt and a score. The response carries the shared envelope:
``items``, ``items_total``, ``items_returned``, ``truncated``,
``next_cursor`` and ``provenance`` naming the index identity, lanes,
routes and producers. ``include_provenance=true`` additionally shows,
on every item, its own provenance and a null locator with its typed
reason - what the response-level provenance already states is folded
away by default.

* ``kinds`` - ``"symbol"``, ``"metadata"``, or both (default).
* ``cursor`` - a ``next_cursor`` this endpoint issued earlier. It is
  opaque: do not parse or construct one. A cursor presented after the
  served index changed fails with ``cursor_stale`` naming both
  identities; a malformed one fails with ``cursor_invalid``.
* ``max_items`` / ``max_bytes`` - the response budget (0 = default). The
  effective budget, including any server-side clamp, is reported back.
* ``items_total`` is ``null`` with a typed reason when the candidate cap
  was reached, rather than reporting a count that is not a total.

An ``id`` from here resolves at ``compact_symbol`` or ``compact_metadata``
without transformation.

tools.name: compact_symbol
tools.description:
Look up or page BSL symbols, bodies excluded unless asked for.

Items carry the symbol name, kind, export flag, execution context, owning
module and an exact line range that slices back to exactly that symbol.
``include_body`` is off by default because a body is unbounded and is what
blows a context budget; ``search_function`` keeps its own defaults.

``item_id`` resolves an identifier issued by any compact endpoint.
``module_path`` is a case-insensitive substring filter on the canonical
module path, applied during candidate generation.

tools.name: compact_call
tools.description:
Call edges for a symbol, in one direction, under an explicit budget.

Each item is one edge: caller and callee identifiers, the callee's
resolution state (``resolved`` / ``unresolved`` / ``ambiguous`` - a
platform method is not in the index and says so), and the call-site
locator. A handler passed by name carries ``via`` (``notify_description`` /
``idle_handler``). ``direction`` is ``callees``, ``callers`` or ``both``; ``depth``
is bounded by a documented server maximum.

The response carries a ``traversal`` marker naming which bound stopped it
(``max_nodes`` / ``max_edges`` / ``timeout_ms``) or ``null``, and issues a
``next_cursor`` whenever edges remain.

tools.name: compact_metadata
tools.description:
Page metadata objects with bounded member lists.

This is how a configuration-wide question is answered here: page it. Items
carry the canonical path, type, name, synonym and a bounded member list
with ``members_total`` beside it, so a caller can always tell whether the
list was bounded. ``object_type`` filters during candidate generation
rather than after retrieval. A member list that alone crosses
``max_bytes`` (the default is 32 KB; ``max_members`` up to 200) is cut
to the prefix that fits and named in ``elided_fields`` - raise
``max_bytes`` or page the members through ``get_metadata_details``.
``include_provenance=true`` shows each item's own provenance and null
locator; by default the response-level provenance carries them once.

tools.name: reindex
tools.description:
Trigger re-indexing of the 1C configuration (runs in background).

Uses the same phased orchestrator as startup: ``metadata`` is always
indexed first, followed by ``code`` and ``help``. Returns immediately;
monitor progress via ``stats()`` under the ``indexing`` key.

* ``force=False`` — **incremental**: every phase invokes
  ``_index_file_list`` with the full on-disk list and the tracker
  classifies each file by SHA-256 content hash into
  ``new`` / ``modified`` / ``unchanged`` / ``deleted``. Unchanged
  files are skipped; modified files have their old chunks deleted
  before the new ones are embedded; deleted files have their chunks
  removed from the vector store — which removes their full-text rows
  with them — and their tracker rows cleared. Requires
  ``INCREMENTAL_INDEXING=true`` (default). When
  ``INCREMENTAL_INDEXING=false`` the legacy ``count() == 0`` skip is
  preserved and no tracker reconciliation happens.
* ``force=True`` — every lane re-runs unconditionally inside a **fresh
  generation** in which every source file is classified ``new``. Nothing
  is carried over, and the published generation keeps serving, intact,
  until the forced generation seals and publishes: a forced rebuild no
  longer wipes what the tools are reading from (CODE-COMP-005 AC7).

When another process already owns the project's writer lease the call
returns the typed result ``writer_busy``, naming the owner and the
in-flight ``generation_id``; no second build starts and no run is queued.

Per-phase counts in ``stats().data.indexing.per_phase[*].counts``
include ``new``, ``modified``, ``unchanged``, ``deleted``, and the
legacy ``vector_indexed`` (files for which at least one chunk was
successfully written during this run).

tools.name: stats
tools.description:
Get server statistics: document counts, embedding provider, index status.

The ``indexing`` key exposes the orchestrator snapshot with the
current phase, per-phase status (``pending``/``running``/``completed``/
``failed``/``disabled``), start/completion timestamps, and any
phase-local error. Phases switched off via ``INDEX_METADATA`` /
``INDEX_CODE`` / ``INDEX_HELP`` are reported as ``disabled`` and are
never scheduled.

Each entry under ``indexing.per_phase[<phase>].counts`` carries
integer fields ``new``, ``modified``, ``unchanged``, ``deleted`` (from
the tracker-driven incremental pass) and the legacy ``vector_indexed``
(files with at least one chunk successfully embedded this run), plus
any phase-specific extras such as ``details_indexed`` / ``xsd_generated``.

``indexing.last_incremental_at`` is an ISO-8601 timestamp of the most
recent **successful** incremental run (force=False). It is ``null``
until the first such run completes. ``force=true`` rebuilds do not
update this timestamp.

``indexing.last_outcome`` is how the most recent finished run ended --
``completed``, ``failed``, ``cancelled`` (a shutdown was requested) or
``degraded`` (the run published or skipped while a vector lane still
cannot be written; ``indexing.error`` names the lane(s) and the
remediation is ``reindex(force=true)``) -- and is ``null`` until the
first run of this process finishes. A run that ends before its first
phase, while it is still taking the inventory or resolving its builder,
reports ``failed`` there and names the failure in ``indexing.error``
rather than leaving the snapshot describing a build that is no longer
happening.

``indexing.sources`` lists every configuration source the run
encountered (CODE-SAVED-1187299): the configuration being indexed, and
any configuration nested inside it such as a supplier configuration
under ``Ext/ParentConfigurations``. Each entry carries the
``source_id``, its ``root`` relative to the configuration being indexed,
its ``kind``, whether it was ``processed`` or ``skipped``, the
``reason`` for a skip -- ``policy_excluded`` for a policy decision and
``source_unreadable:<error>`` for one that could not be read, so the two
are never confused -- and per-source ``counts``.
``indexing.source_policy`` is the effective include/exclude decision per
kind, and ``indexing.current_source`` names the source being processed
right now, so progress is observable mid-run and is ``null`` once the
phase is terminal.

``index_lanes`` carries, per derived-state lane (``forms``,
``symbols``), the content-table row count, the full-text row count and a
``complete`` / ``incomplete`` / ``disabled`` / ``unavailable`` verdict.
It is derived from stored counts, so a populated content table beside an
empty search index is visible without issuing a search, and a phase is
never reported ``completed`` while one of its lanes is incomplete
(CODE-ERR-TILDA-05).

``sub_index_gates`` carries, per SQLite sub-index, the outcome of the
integrity and coverage gates that run before a phase is marked
``completed``: ``passed``, ``failed`` (with the failing checks named
under ``reasons``), or ``not_run``. A store that was never gated stays
``not_run`` so it is never mistaken for a clean one.

``embedding_provider`` carries the typed embedding-provider state
(CODE-ERR-TILDA-04): the resolved ``provider`` (``remote``/``local``), the
``status`` (``ok`` / ``unreachable`` / ``unauthorized`` /
``model_not_found`` / ``budget_exceeded`` / ``not_configured``, and
``unknown`` before the first provider call), the ``selection_reason`` the
provider was reached by, the ``model``, the ``endpoint_host`` for a remote
provider, and -- for a local one -- ``memory_budget_mb``,
``estimated_model_mb`` and the sampled ``process_rss_mb``. It never
contains the API key in any form.

``generation`` carries the immutable-generation lifecycle
(CODE-COMP-005): the ``published`` generation id with its publish
timestamp, per-lane typed state and ``new``/``changed``/``deleted``/
``unchanged`` counts; the ``in_flight`` generation and its typed state
while a build is running; ``last_failed`` with the typed ``reason`` of the
most recent non-published generation; the ``retained`` ids available for
rollback; the ``pinned`` generations a reader still holds; the writer
``lease``; and the ``manifest`` status, which reports a typed
``manifest_unreadable`` / ``manifest_schema_unsupported`` /
``manifest_inconsistent`` rather than raising. The section is read without
the writer lease, so it never blocks a build.

``release`` carries the release identity (CODE-ERR-TILDA-20260804-HTTP-OPS):
the ``version`` and ``build_digest`` of the running build, the
``index_layout`` range of on-disk layouts it can open, the ``source`` the
identity was resolved from (``manifest_file`` / ``environment`` /
``source``) and, when ``MCP_IMAGE_REF`` is set, whether that deployment
reference is immutable and matches this build.

``sessions`` carries the transport session bounds and their counters:
``current`` / ``peak`` sessions, ``reclaimed_idle`` /
``reclaimed_lifetime`` / ``rejected_cap``, and the effective ``limits``
(idle TTL, maximum lifetime, concurrent cap, cleanup interval) with the
``mode`` they run in (``enforce`` or ``report``).

``vector_store_health`` carries the vector-store optimize and integrity
state. ``terminal`` is ``null`` on a healthy process, or the
``{collection, reason, detail}`` of the first store that reached a
terminal state (``store_corruption`` / ``write_failures_exceeded``).
``collections[<name>]`` reports, per lane: whether optimize is
``enabled``, the ``last_outcome`` and ``last_elapsed_sec`` of its merge,
the documents still ``pending_docs`` for the next merge, the current
``write_health`` and ``terminal_reason``, the
``consecutive_write_failures`` against the configured
``write_failure_threshold``, the effective ``write_mode``
(``insert``/``upsert``) with its ``insert_fallbacks`` count, and whether
the lane is ``quarantined``.

tools.name: plugin_state
tools.description:
Report the plugin subsystem: what is loaded, what it costs, which epoch.

Every file, the hooks and tables it declares, the classification of each
hook, whether it is enabled, the error that disabled it, the failure count,
the time accumulated in it, the order the files run in, the current epoch,
and the digest the derived-state hooks contribute to the generation
fingerprint.

tools.name: unpack_ordinary_form
tools.description:
Read one standalone ordinary-form ``Form.bin`` into an editable workspace.

An ordinary form is exported as a binary container, unlike a managed
form's ``Ext/Form.xml``. Do not edit ``Form.bin`` directly and do not read
it as XML: unpack it here, edit the payload, build it back with
``build_ordinary_form``.

The workspace holds ``payload/`` - the container's entries verbatim, and
the only thing a rebuild reads - plus ``decoded/``, derived views for
reading (``form.json``, the layout as JSON-compatible data; ``module.bsl``,
the form module). Editing a derived view is refused by the build rather
than silently dropped.

What the layout can say: the brace tree is positional. It is structurally
parseable and it names no elements. Named element trees (``*.elem.json``)
come only from high-level extraction of a whole CF / CFE / EPF, where the
surrounding metadata supplies the names. Nothing here is invented.

``include`` selects a bounded preview - ``summary`` (default, paths only),
``structure``, ``module`` or ``all`` - and ``max_chars`` bounds each one.
The full decoded views are always on disk, whatever the answer carries.

tools.name: build_ordinary_form
tools.description:
Write an ordinary-form workspace back to a ``Form.bin``, and verify it.

Verification re-reads what was just written, with the same code that reads
the original, and compares the *logical payload* - entry names, sizes and
SHA-256 of the payload bytes. It deliberately does not compare the final
binaries: the container records carry write timestamps, so a rebuilt
``Form.bin`` differs byte for byte from its source even when nothing
changed. ``binary_identical`` reports that fact; ``verification.status`` is
what says whether the form survived.

Nothing is replaced silently: an existing ``output_path`` is refused unless
``overwrite`` is set, and a failed build leaves the previous file in place.

tools.name: plugin_reload
tools.description:
Re-read the plugin directory without restarting, and start a new epoch.

Every file is read again and the set in force is replaced in one step; if
any file no longer loads, nothing is replaced, the previous set stays in
force and the response names the file and the reason. A call-scoped hook
takes effect on the next call. A derived-state hook does not apply
retroactively - it shapes the next build, and the generation that is
published keeps serving until then. Outstanding continuation tokens are
refused after a reload that changed the set, because the index identity they
are bound to carries the plugin epoch.
